wins.text: Q2 revenue of $12.9B came in above the high end of guidance, driven by strength in both client and data center segments
Excluding ~$1B in one-time impairment and period costs, non-GAAP gross margin would have been 37.5% and EPS $0.10, both ahead of Q2 guidance
Intel Products revenue of $11.8B with operating profit of $2.7B (23% margin); CCG up 3% QoQ and DCAI above expectations despite 5% sequential decline
18A reached key milestone with start of production wafers in Arizona ahead of Panther Lake Q4 launch; Xeon 6 selected as host node for NVIDIA DGX B300 AI accelerated systems
Raised ~$900M through Mobileye offering and on track to close Altera stake sale to Silver Lake in Q3, shoring up balance sheet

risks.text: Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 29.7% due to ~$800M noncash impairment/accelerated depreciation on excess prior-gen tools and ~$200M one-time period costs; GAAP charges of $1.9B mostly from severance
Q3 gross margin guided to ~36%, pressured by Lunar Lake memory-in-package mix headwind, early Panther Lake ramp costs, and increased tariff-related costs
Intel 7 capacity remains tight through H2 2025, constraining foundry revenue; Intel Foundry operating loss of $3.2B in Q2

Below-seasonal H2 2025 revenue expected as management believes prior quarters benefited from customer tariff-hedging pull-forward; Q3 revenue guided to $12.6B–$13.6B vs. typical high-single-digit sequential growth

Server CPU market share under pressure with ASPs down 8% YoY per 10-Q; ARM competition cited as a growing threat; management acknowledges multi-threading capability mistakes and need for new data center leadership

guidance_items.detail: Q3 guided to $12.6B–$13.6B (midpoint $13.1B), down 2% to up 6% sequentially; below-seasonal H2 flagged due to potential tariff pull-forward in prior quarters
Q3 non-GAAP gross margin guided to ~36%, down from Q2's underlying 37.5% (ex-charges), due to Lunar Lake mix, Panther Lake ramp costs, and tariffs
Q3 non-GAAP EPS guided to breakeven, same as original Q2 guidance
2025 gross CapEx now ~$18B; net CapEx $8B–$11B; 2026 gross and net CapEx expected lower than 2025, down ~$5B YTD from start of year
2025 OpEx target of $17B and 2026 OpEx target of $16B reaffirmed; on track to reach 75,000 employee headcount by year-end

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Server CPU ASP decline of 8% YoY due to competitive pricing pressure (raised from 10-Q, not discussed in prepared remarks)
ARM server competition and potential for ARM to capture over half the server market
Sustainability of foundry strategy if Intel 14A is abandoned — whether the foundry business can survive on 18A internal volumes alone
